stem:
Most plants are C3 plants and are so-called because their first photosynthetic product is a three carbon compound.

The enzyme ribulose bisphosphate carboxylase/oxygenase (rubisco) catalyses the fixation of carbon dioxide in the Calvin cycle and is used by both C3 and C4 plants.

Each molecule is made up of eight large polypeptides and eight small polypeptides. Fig. 2.1 shows a side view of the molecule.

{{figure:figure_2_1.png}}

Fig. 2.1

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Outline how the biochemistry of C4 plants differs from that of C3 plants.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State why rubisco is said to have quaternary structure.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: Explain what makes a molecule such as rubisco soluble.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The active sites of rubisco accept ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP) and **either** carbon dioxide **or** oxygen and can catalyse the two reactions shown below.

*either*

$RuBP + CO_2 \rightarrow \text{unstable intermediate compound} \rightarrow 2GP \text{ (PGA)}$

*or*

$RuBP + 2O_2 \rightarrow \text{unstable intermediate compound} \rightarrow GP \text{ (PGA)} + 2CO_2$

Explain the consequences to the plant of the reaction involving oxygen.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
In the absence of light, rubisco changes shape from an active form to an inactive form.

Explain why rubisco does **not** need to be in an active form in the absence of light.
